rigLog.title: Full rig log
rigLog.subtitle: Complete line build — 3 gates + log

gateA.title: Gate A — Anchors approved
gateA.a1Detail: Visual and mechanical. Rock/tree/bolts/A-frame — each has its own criteria. If you doubt anything, do not proceed.
gateA.a2: Redundancy verified (2 independent points each side)
gateA.a2Detail: Minimum 2 independent points per side, so if one fails the other holds. No redundancy, no build.
gateA.a3: SPOF not found (no single point of failure)
gateA.a3Detail: Walk the whole system with your eyes. One element = one fall? Do you see any single carabiner, single knot without backup? Remove.

gateB.title: Gate B — System before tensioning
gateB.description: After anchor build, transport, and rig before tension.
gateB.b1: Main and backup independently connected (no shared single point of failure)
gateB.b1Detail: They may share redundant anchoring material — e.g. spanset and rope both threaded through two shackles, masterpoint on one, backup on the other. What they must not share is a single element whose failure drops both. Per ISA:21 §3.10 a masterpoint serves mainline and backup together.
gateB.b2Detail: Weblock is progress capture for Buckingham system. Tie-off tied, visually checked. Without tie-off = fatal.
gateB.b3: Backup functional (loose, but not resting on ground)
gateB.b3Detail: Back-up must hang freely (to catch on failure), but not so loose it lies on the ground. Test with weight.

gateC.title: Gate C — Line approved for walking
gateC.description: Second pair of eyes. Before highliner mounts.
gateC.c1: Second check done (second pair of eyes, both anchors)
gateC.c1Detail: Another team member walks both anchors independently. When the rigger no longer sees their mistakes after hours of building, second eye finds them.
gateC.c2Detail: Leash: correct length for the line, certified ring encompassing both lines, knot with tail min 10 cm.
gateC.c3: Rescue plan and who does it
gateC.c3Detail: Out loud: who, with what, where's the gear. Without rescue plan no one climbs on. Suspension trauma = 5 min limit.

reason.treeAnchor: Tree anchor — requires padding and inspection

item.harnessDetail: Doubled buckle, waist belt above hips, leg loops tight. Visual check before mounting.
item.leashDetail: Certified ring must encompass mainline and back-up. If only one → mainline failure drops you under the other.
item.anchorDetail: Redundancy (min 2 points), leg angle < 45°, no sharp edges. Visual check on both sides.
item.backupDetail: Backup ring or PAS on harness. Physically hang on backup alone, verify it holds.
item.rescuePlanDetail: Who will do the rescue, with what (rope, ascender, pulley), how long to reach you. Verbal check with team.
item.weblockTieoffDetail: Final step of weblock rigging. Without tie-off, webbing can slip out under vibration. Visual check on both sides.
item.nylonRuleDetail: Mainline, back-up and leash must all be nylon. Polyester or Dyneema on short HL = anchor peak over 12 kN.
item.windDetail: Ventusky / Windy / actual feel. Above 30 km/h detape starts, above 60 km/h every highline fails.
item.storm: No storms expected in next 2 hours
item.stormDetail: Radar (Meteoradar, Windy). Storm approach + rain = electrostatic discharge in UHMWPE, plasma 5000-15000°C. Derig.
item.treeAnchorDetail: Diameter > 30 cm, healthy tree, undamaged bark, padding between webbing and bark. If unsure — do not anchor.

lineSafety.sessionEmpty: You haven't checked any item. Save check with a note anyway?

isaSafety.title: ISA Safety Companion
isaSafety.subtitle: Highline safety reference
isaSafety.disclaimer: Based on ISA:21 (2023) and related standards. This app provides recommendations, the final decision is always yours.

bowline.title: Bowline never for HL anchor
bowline.summary: Critical rule — bowline loosens under cyclic loading
bowline.bw1: Do not use bowline on the anchor
bowline.bw1Detail: Repeated loading and unloading gradually loosens the knot. Risk of untying under load — fatal.
bowline.bw2Detail: Figure-8 re-traced holds under cyclic loading. Standard for highline anchor.
bowline.bw3Detail: After tightening the knot, tail must be at least 10 cm (recommended 15+ cm). Shorter = risk of pulling through the knot.

weblockTieoff.title: Weblock always with tie-off
weblockTieoff.summary: Final step of weblock rigging — without it, webbing slips out
weblockTieoff.wt1Detail: After threading webbing through the weblock, tie off the tail (typically overhand + backup knot). Without it, webbing can gradually slip out.
weblockTieoff.wt2Detail: Before walking, check tie-off on both weblocks. Part of buddy check.
weblockTieoff.wt3Detail: Vibration + gravity tensioning webbing = gradual slip from weblock. Especially on long lines with wind. Fatal if fails during walk.

electrostatic.title: Electrostatic Discharge Warning
electrostatic.summary: Newest ISA safety warning (12/2025) — plasma arcs during storms
electrostatic.e1Detail: Do not wait for the first lightning strike. Plasma arcs can form between wet webbing segments even before the main storm. Watch radar (Windy, Meteoradar).
electrostatic.e2Detail: Melts at 150°C. Plasma arcs 5000-15000°C cause immediate failure. For storm-prone locations, prefer nylon or polyester.
electrostatic.e3: Consider tapeless setup for storm locations
electrostatic.e3Detail: Dry webbing under tape acts as insulator, wet segment beside it as conductor — arc forms between them. Without tape, energy dissipates evenly.
electrostatic.e4Detail: Remove all tape. Look for burn marks, melted fibers, discoloration. Hidden damage under tape may fail under load.
electrostatic.e5Detail: Latest one in CZ 2024. Do not ignore — this is a real risk. Details in the ISA Warning document (link in source).

twoAttachments.title: Two Attachments Rule
twoAttachments.summary: Critical safety rule for rigging, rescue and highline walk
twoAttachments.t1: Always min 2 independent attachments to the line/rope
twoAttachments.t1Detail: During any operation (rigging, taping, rescue, ascending) you must have 2 independent attachment points. Failure of one = the other holds.
twoAttachments.t2Detail: Before disconnecting primary attachment, load-test the secondary. Sit, weight, verify it holds. Only then disconnect primary.
twoAttachments.t3Detail: Highliner is connected to mainline via leash + backup ring to backup line. Mainline failure = backup catches. Never just the leash.
twoAttachments.t4: For rescue: primary rope + backup PAS
twoAttachments.t4Detail: When moving on the line (rescue, self-rescue), your primary connection (Tibloc, Micro Traxion) plus backup PAS (personal anchor system) on harness.
twoAttachments.t5: Also applies to anchor connections (2026 update)
twoAttachments.t5Detail: Must be 2 independent shackles between BFK and rigging plate — not 1 double-wrapped. Buddy check test: "If one connection failed, would the system stay intact?" Roberto 20.8.2026 Mistake Line.

buddyCheck.title: Buddy Check
buddyCheck.summary: Checklist before every walk onto a highline
buddyCheck.b1: Harness — correctly worn, buckles doubled back
buddyCheck.b1Detail: Check: gear loops OK, leg loops tight, waist belt above hips. Buckle must be doubled back (thread the strap back through).
buddyCheck.b2Detail: Re-traced Figure-8 through harness belay loop. Tail min 10 cm. Barrel knot backup not required but recommended for Bowline / Flemish bend.
buddyCheck.b3Detail: Ring must encompass both mainline and backup line. If only one → mainline failure drops highliner under backup line = death.
buddyCheck.b4Detail: Backup ring or backup PAS. Physically hang on the backup alone, verify it holds.
buddyCheck.b5: Helmet — if above 5 m or hard anchor
buddyCheck.b5Detail: Personal choice under 5 m over soft ground. Above 5 m or over hard terrain = mandatory. Head trauma cannot be softened by stretch.
buddyCheck.b6Detail: This is not formality. Verbal spoken OK = closure of the check. If buddy hesitates = STOP, redo.

suspensionTrauma.title: Suspension Trauma Awareness
suspensionTrauma.summary: Critical info for rescue situations (⚠️ NOT a rescue guide)
suspensionTrauma.s1: Unconscious highliner in harness = 5 minutes critical
suspensionTrauma.s1Detail: Harness acts as tourniquet. Blood in legs becomes deoxygenated. At 15 min = death even for healthy individual without injury.
suspensionTrauma.s2Detail: If conscious and moving, they can shift harness. But still: the faster down, the better. Do not do routine rescue.
suspensionTrauma.s3: After ground extraction: NEVER lay flat immediately
suspensionTrauma.s3Detail: Toxic blood floods heart → cardiac arrhythmia / arrest. Sit up slowly, W-position (knees to chest), then recovery position.
suspensionTrauma.s4: This is NOT a rescue guide — call emergency services
suspensionTrauma.s4Detail: Highline rescue requires training. Do not activate based on the app. Primarily call emergency (112 EU, 911 US). This card is awareness — so you know time is short.

rigWorkflow.title: Complete rig workflow
rigWorkflow.summary: Full tree of line building from home planning to leaving
rigWorkflow.rw1Detail: From anchors (0-2) through main (3-4), backup (5), tension (6), checks (7) to walk-ready (8). Each phase has checkpoints.
rigWorkflow.rw2Detail: A: anchors approved (SNARE SANE). B: system before tension (main + backup + weblock). C: line approved to walk (rescue plan + buddy check).
rigWorkflow.rw3Detail: Material (ISA cert, RLT status) / Safety (rescue plan, communication) / People (competence, buddy check). Applied across all phases.
rigWorkflow.rw4Detail: Must be 2 independent shackles (main + backup separate connection). Double-wrapped single shackle looks like two, but is still single point failure. Classic buddy check trap. Roberto 20.8.2026 Mistake Line commentary.
rigWorkflow.rw5Detail: Consolidated point (double ring / rigging plate / doubled sling) where main and backup terminate. NOT separated anchors (hidden dependency). Nicolas Ospina 31.5.2025.

novice.title: Starting out? Read this first
novice.summary: Basic rules for beginners before you go anywhere
novice.n1: Highline is NOT DIY from an app
novice.n1Detail: The app is reference material, not a first-rig guide. False sense of safety from an app = deadly. Training is essential.
novice.n2Detail: The first years you learn from experienced people. Go build with them as an observer, then a helper, only then as lead rigger. Takes years.
novice.n3Detail: There are active groups worldwide — Facebook groups, personal contacts. Check the Community section in Settings for a list.
novice.n4Detail: ISA (International Slackline Association) certifies instructors. Rigger Cert = international standard.
novice.n5Detail: Longline < 20 cm above ground. Then trickline. Highline only after years of training and with someone experienced overseeing.

isa21Limits.title: ISA:21 Force Limits
isa21Limits.summary: Key safety limits for highline systems

serene.title: SERENE
serene.strongDetail: Anchor holds min 2× expected peak load. Target: 48 kN primary, 24 kN secondary.
serene.equalizedDetail: Load evenly distributed across all points. Sliding-X actively, BFK statically.
serene.redundantDetail: If 1 point fails, rest holds the load. Min 2 independent attachment points.
serene.efficientDetail: Angles between legs < 60° ideal, < 90° maximum. Above 120° = catastrophic.
serene.noExtensionDetail: If 1 leg fails, masterpoint stays in place → no shock load. Backup / limiting knots.
serene.masterpointDetail: Always consolidated masterpoint where both main and backup terminate (double ring / rigging plate / doubled sling). Overwrites old "main and backup separate" rule. Nicolas Ospina 31.5.2025.

snareSane.title: SNARE SANE
snareSane.strengthDetail: Anchor holds min 2× expected peak load. Calculate max load (peak fall × safety factor 2).
snareSane.noAbrasionDetail: No sharp edges in load path. Visual check, padding at sharp edges.
snareSane.redundancyDetail: If 1 component fails, anchor still holds. Min 2 independent points.
snareSane.equalizationDetail: Load evenly distributed. Sliding-X actively, BFK statically.
snareSane.smallAnglesDetail: Angle between anchor legs < 60° ideal. 90° = per-leg 71%, 120° = 100%, > 120° = catastrophic.
snareSane.noExtensionDetail: Failure of one leg must not cause shock load. Backup / limiting knots.
snareSane.singleCauseFailuresDetail: Material redundancy ≠ structural redundancy. 5 categories of common-mode failures: rock (bolts in one flake) / material (BFK with wrong rope) / sling (dual-core abrasion) / weather (storms) / rodents (chews). Julian 1.9.2025.

nylonRule.title: Sub-40m Nylon Rule
nylonRule.summary: Webbing material compatibility with line length
nylonRule.hint: Sub-40m highline = mainline + backup + leash all PA (nylon). Static materials (PES, UHMWPE) generate 2-3× higher peak forces = risk of exceeding ISA:21 limit 12 kN.

wind.title: Wind Advisory
wind.summary: ISA thresholds for rig / derig decision
wind.hint: Watch Ventusky, Windy or Open-Meteo. Storm approach = derig immediately (electrostatic risk).

rlt.title: Recommended Lifetime (RLT)
rlt.summary: Recommended webbing lifetime by type and material
rlt.hint: Days = exposure to environment (UV, rain), NOT from manufacture date. Storage doesn't count.

forgottenLeash.title: Forgotten Leash
forgottenLeash.summary: Most fatal recurring failure in highline
forgottenLeash.fl1Detail: Documented fatalities: Brazil 26.7.2025 (SUPER experienced guy forgot tie-in), Slovenia 2023 (permanent nerve damage). Most common cause of serious HL injuries.
forgottenLeash.fl2Detail: Experienced riggers are at highest risk. Muscle memory = 'I know what I'm doing, no check needed' → one forgotten session restart is enough.
forgottenLeash.fl3Detail: Break (water / WC / phone / rescue) → return to line WITHOUT leash. Critical transition moment.
forgottenLeash.fl4Detail: Not just first session. Before every entry onto the line = physically verify leash + PAS by hand.
forgottenLeash.fl5Detail: Say out loud 'am I tied in?' → 'yes, verified'. Requires active cognitive check, not muscle memory.

masterpoint.title: Masterpoint doctrine (ISA 2025+)
masterpoint.summary: Always consolidated masterpoint, not separated anchors
masterpoint.mp1Detail: Always consolidated masterpoint where both main and backup terminate. Nicolas Ospina 31.5.2025 (ISA Certified Rigger) cites ISA guidelines.
masterpoint.mp2Detail: Double ring / rigging plate / doubled sling. Criterion: one common point for both main and backup.
masterpoint.mp3Detail: Hidden dependency. Roberto: 'if you lose main shackle, you lose main line AND main anchor too.'
masterpoint.mp4Detail: Reduces extension on failure. Simplifies inspection (one point = clear check). Reduces rigger cognitive load.
masterpoint.mp5Detail: Old: 'main and backup should be separate.' NOT VALID in 2025+. Validates TZ post-cert learning from Ostrov 16-18.8.2026.

bfkSlidingX.title: When BFK, when Sliding-X
bfkSlidingX.summary: Decision framework for longline + wind exposure
bfkSlidingX.bsx1Detail: HL < 200-300m length. Vertically parallel points. Stable load direction (no wind-driven asymmetric load).
bfkSlidingX.bsx2Detail: HL > 200-300m (wind-driven asymmetric load can collapse BFK). Wind exposure. Non-parallel points. Weak or questionable rock.
bfkSlidingX.bsx3Detail: 'A BFK is sufficient as long as one of the ropes could get cut and the rest of the anchor remains above the 24kN MBS.' — Sascha Grill 28.2.2026.
bfkSlidingX.bsx4Detail: 'Anything greater than 200-300m, I'm going with sliding X.' — Roberto De Oliveira 1.3.2026 (800m longline failure case).

alWeblockCorrosion.title: Al weblock corrosion in perma-rig
alWeblockCorrosion.summary: Active ISA incident 2026 — casting defect crack after 1-2 years
alWeblockCorrosion.awc1Detail: ISA actively addressing (x-ray plan proposed by ISA Safety Commission). 2 documented cases: Roberto 20.3.2026 heavily used perma-rig weblock, Purelock 3-4 months.
alWeblockCorrosion.awc2Detail: Al weblock in perma-rig with humidity → casting defect crack after 1-2 years. Nothing happened, but weblock fully damaged. Early warning.
alWeblockCorrosion.awc3Detail: Perma-rig weblock ROTATE every 6 months (don't leave in one spot 1+ year). Steel weblock preferred for perma-rig in humid environment.
alWeblockCorrosion.awc4Detail: Coastal / marine sites require more aggressive re-inspection cycle. X-ray inspection recommended for suspect Al weblocks.

vortexCaveat.title: Vortex leash ring — tape gate shut!
vortexCaveat.vc1Detail: Sascha 10.7.2025: 'I stepped on the gate and it opened, I heard from a friend that they stepped on it while tandeming and even UNCLIPPED the line!'
vortexCaveat.vc2Detail: Only for tandem highlining (when you need a larger ring). ALWAYS tape gate shut (electrical tape over gate).
vortexCaveat.vc3Detail: 2× standard Slacktivity Highline Ring instead of Vortex. Adds redundancy + removes gate risk.
vortexCaveat.vc4Detail: Verify tape integrity. Never step on gate side of ring. Buddy check — second pair of eyes checks gate.
